$comment: Which documents govern which paths. Read by scripts/verify-context-routes.sh:
a change under `paths` must cite one of its `read` documents, in a commit
message on the branch or in the Agent Note it carries.
This is the mechanical half of rules/fuentes.md. The prose states the
precedence; this file makes forgetting to look a failing gate.
Adapt to your repo. A route with paths that never match is dead weight, and
a route that fires on every change trains people to paste the citation
without reading — keep them narrow and few, and add one only when you can
Patterns: exact paths, fnmatch globs, or `dir/**` for a whole subtree.

routes.why: Business rules decide verdicts, and their trade-offs are already recorded. An external report describes a symptom; it does not repeal a decision.
A migration changes what the data means for everyone downstream, and it cannot be taken back by editing a file.
Changing a gate changes what the harness is willing to let through. Weakening one is the change that hides every other.
